model_source: OAK-Drive-Sync src/sim/kinematics.py + config/sim_rig.yaml (digital twin); identical formulas in camera_pose.py

units.angle: deg (degrees) in all parameters and axis values; radians only internally

frame.name: specimen frame
frame.origin: centre of the weld seam on the specimen mid-plane (half thickness, half width, weld height)
frame.x: normal of the specimen FRONT face, pointing toward cam1 (cam2 looks at the back face from -x)
frame.y: across the specimen width (= z cross x); parallel to the ring/tilt axes
frame.z: up, along the specimen length axis (specimen clamped vertically, weld seam horizontal)
frame.faces: front face at x = +t/2 = +12.5, back face at x = -12.5 (t = 25); weld bead adds ~2 mm (placeholder)

axes.name: a
axes.drive: GPIO stepper on Raspberry Pi 5 (cam1:a, cam2:a)
axes.variable: h_mm = height of the ring axis (pivot) above the weld centre
axes.range_status: PLACEHOLDER - real stroke not yet provided; steps/mm unknown
axes.parent: base (rig frame, fixed to the machine; equals the specimen frame when the weld is at z = 0)

axes.name: b
axes.drive: Tinkerforge Silent Stepper Bricklet 2.0 -> worm 1-start / wheel 60 z -> pinion 16 z on internal ring-gear segment 120 z (m = 2); ~0.8 deg carriage tilt per motor revolution
axes.axis_direction: parallel to y through the pivot P = (s*(t/2 + D_pivot), 0, h); positive rotation tilts the optical axis upward (+z) for both cameras
axes.range_status: estimated from CAD (rollers on guide-ring rim, rim +-61.5 deg, teeth +-78 deg); not measured; limit switches not final

cam2.looks_at: back face (-x side), mirror of cam1

transformation_chain: T_a(h) = translation (s*(t/2 + D_pivot), 0, h) -> pivot P on the ring axis; D_pivot = working_distance - lens_to_pivot = 262 mm
T_b(theta) = rotation about +/-y through P such that forward d = (-s*cos(theta), 0, sin(theta)), up = (s*sin(theta), 0, cos(theta))
T_cam = translation by -lens_to_pivot along d -> optical centre O = P - 38*d
optional image roll about d: cam1 180 deg (mounted upside down per IMU calibration, UNVERIFIED), cam2 0 deg

camera_mount_to_optical_center.description: Optical centre lies on the optical axis BEHIND the ring axis; the optical axis always passes through the ring axis (CAD: 3 mm miss distance).
camera_mount_to_optical_center.working_distance_definition: optical centre -> flat front face along the optical axis at tilt 0
camera_mount_to_optical_center.note: 38 mm is measured in CAD from the ring axis to the front glass / centre lens of the OAK-D PoE enclosure (37.7-39.7 mm). The true entrance pupil of the IMX586 module lies a few mm further back (unknown). The Mitsuba setup uses 0.21 m; the operator gives ~0.30 m for current experiments - use the measured value of your reference photo.
camera_mount_to_optical_center.camera_intrinsics_hint: IMX586, 1920x1080, HFOV 67.3 deg per the Mitsuba project, VFOV 41.06 deg derived for 16:9 (the twin uses the same values)

pose_formula.up: u = (s*sin(theta), 0, cos(theta))  [then rotate 180 deg about d for cam1 if the upside-down mount is confirmed]
pose_formula.weld_centred_tilt: h = -(WD - L)*tan(theta) keeps the optical axis on the weld centre
pose_formula.symbols: s = +1 cam1 / -1 cam2, t = 25, WD = 300, L = 38, theta = tilt_deg

default_geometry_mm.weld: DV butt weld (UP), horizontal at z = 0; bead placeholder 2 mm high, 19 mm wide

specimen_frame.stl_alignment_hint: align the 3D scan so that the weld centreline lies on the y axis at z = 0, specimen length along z, front face toward +x (cam1 side)

uv_lamps.current_setup_note: Two UV lamps per specimen side are FIXED (not on the camera carriage, not enough space) and placed to illuminate the whole field. Their poses are not in any CAD/config available here - must be measured.

cad_reference_original_design.status: historical: original CAD design where the lamps rode on the camera carriage; NOT the current setup

lamps.name: uv_left
lamps.emission: approximately parallel to the optical axis (dummy disc ~120 mm diameter; emission sign inferred)

lamps.name: uv_right
lamps.emission: approximately parallel to the optical axis

probe_9_2_reference_photo.status: NOMINAL: 'frontal, ~30 cm'. No logged axis values exist for this photo.

weld_centred_tilts_example.note: derived from the model (optical axis stays on the weld centre), not from a logged experiment
